0.2.1.title: An AI assistant can drive it, and a bad edit no longer resets a template
0.2.1.summary: Capstone's templates, settings and queue can be driven by an AI assistant, and an edit it cannot apply is now refused instead of quietly reverting your other settings.
highlights: Capstone can be read and driven by an AI assistant that speaks MCP: templates, output settings, the queue and starting a run.

An edit that cannot be applied is refused and your template is left alone. Before, one bad field could reset the target loudness, warmth, pitch correction and headroom to the Festival defaults and still report success.
Out-of-range values are clamped consistently now, including the limiter character.

0.2.0.title: Cover art, right-click and shareable templates
0.2.0.summary: The queue now looks like your library, every row has a menu, and a template is a file you can send to someone.
highlights: Album art shows next to every file in the queue.
Right-click a row to play it, reveal it, copy its path, re-analyze it or drop it.
Export a template to a file and import one back. No account, no sign-in.
A short tour on first launch, reopenable from the title bar.
Dark and light themes rebuilt for readability: no more unreadable greys or dimmed-out fields.
Version and a support link now sit along the bottom of the window.

0.1.0.title: First release
0.1.0.summary: Drop in a folder of finished tracks and get them back at one consistent volume, with clipped peaks repaired and the tags still on them.
highlights: Everything you process lands on the same loudness target, with a true-peak limiter so nothing distorts on the way there.
Clipped peaks are repaired before anything else touches the file.
Tracks sitting off concert pitch can be corrected, keeping the tempo or moving it with the pitch.
Optional warmth and multiband dynamics, saved into named templates you reuse.
Reads the formats a library is actually made of, writes AIFF, WAV, FLAC, ALAC or MP3, and carries your tags across.
Your originals are never touched: processed files are written somewhere new.
